solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Comic panel oddly going by the rules

indicators.note: done oddly means done in a strange way, so the letters before it are set out in an unusual order

parts.note: all ten letters of these two words are the fodder

explanation.surface: A strip cartoon frame is behaving strangely by following the regulations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' tempts you to take odd letters of 'Comic panel', but that gives too few; here it means 'strangely', the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Compliance is the act of obeying regulations, which is what going by the rules describes.

clue.text: Singer travelling on recent tour

indicators.note: letters that are travelling move about, so they end up in a fresh order

parts.note: all twelve letters of these words are the fodder

explanation.surface: A vocalist has been on the road during a recent concert tour.
explanation.definitionFit: A countertenor is a male singer whose voice reaches the alto range, a specific kind of vocalist.

clue.text: Get up on stage

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to climb onto, as onto a horse
second meaning: to put on or organise, as with a play or an exhibition

explanation.surface: Someone is told to climb up onto the theatre stage.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'on stage' together, but the split falls after 'on'.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both climbing onto a horse or platform and organising a show or campaign.

clue.text: Cut and run without quite finishing

indicators.note: not quite finishing means stopping just short of the end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: to lope is to run with long easy strides

explanation.surface: Someone slashes at something and flees before the job is done.
explanation.walkthrough: LOPE loses its last letter to give LOP.
explanation.definitionFit: To lop is to cut off a branch or limb, so it is a synonym of cut.

clue.text: Go for a small trip on boat

parts.note: taken as written
S is the standard abbreviation for small
a sail is a voyage in a boat

explanation.surface: An invitation to take a short outing on a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go for' looks like an invitation to take the trip; it is the definition, in its sense of attacking.
explanation.definitionFit: To go for someone is to attack them, and to assail is likewise to attack violently.

clue.text: Officer hoodwinks board

parts.note: to con is to trick, so cons means hoodwinks
a board is a flat surface, as is a table

explanation.surface: An official deceives the members of a company's board of directors.
explanation.definitionFit: A constable is a police officer of the lowest rank in Britain.

clue.text: Bar in no time at all is filled by almost everyone

indicators.note: something filled by another thing has that thing placed inside it

parts.note: soon means very shortly, in hardly any time

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter of the word after it is lost

parts.note: all means everyone

explanation.surface: A pub gets packed out with nearly everybody in no time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' looks like it might mean except or prevent; it is the definition, a drinking room.
explanation.definitionFit: A saloon is a bar, as in the saloon bar of a British pub or a Wild West drinking house.

clue.text: Certain artwork somehow generated profits later

indicators.note: somehow suggests some unknown method of rearranging, so the letters come out in another order

parts.note: all twelve letters of these words are the fodder

explanation.surface: A painting eventually earned its owner some money.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-portrait is one particular kind of painting or drawing, one in which the artist depicts themself.

clue.text: Appropriate pressure following endless money-lending

indicators.note: something endless has no end, so the final letter of the word it qualifies goes
following means coming after, so one piece is placed behind the other

parts.note: usury is lending money at high interest
P is the symbol for pressure in physics

explanation.surface: A suitable amount of pressure applied after a loan arrangement keeps going on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' looks like the adjective meaning suitable; it is the verb meaning to seize.
explanation.definitionFit: To appropriate is to take something for yourself without right, which is exactly what to usurp means.

clue.text: Seasonal visitor initially flying east somewhere in America

parts.note: Father Christmas visits once a year, at Christmas

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of the next word is kept

parts.note: the first letter of flying
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: Father Christmas begins his flight eastwards towards a US destination.
explanation.definitionFit: Santa Fe is the state capital of New Mexico, so it is one particular place in America.

clue.text: Artist who can leave a lasting impression on people

definitions.text: Artist who can leave a lasting impression on people

parts.words: Artist who can leave a lasting impression on people
parts.note: surface reading: a painter or performer whose work stays in people's memories
setter's reading: a permanent mark made literally on people's skin with ink

explanation.walkthrough: A 'lasting impression' sounds like a memorable effect; read literally it is a permanent ink design on someone's body.
explanation.definitionFit: This artist works with needles and ink, creating permanent designs in the skin of customers.

clue.text: Alert ping-pong players might execute spin here

definitions.meaning: first meaning: sharp and quick to react

definitions.text: ping-pong players might execute spin here
definitions.meaning: second meaning, read literally: table tennis players put spin by striking the surface of the sphere

explanation.surface: Sharp table tennis players might put spin on a shot at this point.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a cryptic hint: spin is imparted by brushing the surface of the sphere.
explanation.definitionFit: Being quick and competent is an idiom taken from ball games, where good players keep the ball under control.

clue.text: Away side in cricket match?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the ... side is the half of a cricket field on the batter's bat side

explanation.surface: A query about the visiting team in a game of cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Away side' suggests the visiting team, but the clue splits after 'Away'. In cricket the field divides into the off side and the leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: Off as an adverb means gone, and in cricket it names one half of the field, the off side.

clue.text: Smart machine, British in origin

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so this letter goes into the word that follows

parts.note: a root is a source or origin
B is the abbreviation for British

explanation.surface: A clever device that was invented in Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'British in origin' reads as made in Britain, but B goes inside ROOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A robot is an automated machine able to carry out tasks, often called smart when it acts intelligently.

clue.text: The two heads of employment relish trouble

parts.note: both means the two

indicators.note: heads are the tops, so only the first letter of each following word is taken

parts.note: first letter of employment
first letter of relish

explanation.surface: Two department heads in a workplace enjoy causing difficulties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heads of employment' sounds like managers, and 'relish' like enjoying, but both just give first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Bother is a noun for annoyance or difficulty, a synonym of trouble.

clue.text: You're dead right to discard middle bits of soggy sprouts

parts.note: to bin something is to throw it away

indicators.note: middle bits are the central parts, so only the centre letter of each following word is kept

parts.note: the central letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Someone is told they are quite right to throw out the mushy centres of overcooked Brussels sprouts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discard' is not a deletion signal here; it supplies the verb for throwing away.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is shouted when a guess hits the mark, the same as saying the person is exactly correct.

clue.text: Most astute copper put on trial

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a test is a trial

explanation.surface: The sharpest police officer has been sent for trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' suggests a police officer; here it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Cute can mean clever or shrewd, especially in American and Irish usage, so the superlative means most shrewd.

clue.text: Have steak, say, forgoing starter

indicators.note: forgoing the starter means going without the first course, so the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: steak is an example of red flesh food

explanation.surface: A diner orders the steak but skips the first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starter' plays on the first course of a meal, but it means the first letter. MEAT minus M gives EAT.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a meal is to eat it, so have is an everyday synonym here.

clue.text: Vivacious former rideshare worker?

parts.note: ex means former
Uber is a well-known ride-hailing company
a worker ant, a classic crossword sense of worker

explanation.surface: A lively person who used to drive for a taxi-hailing app.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rideshare worker' reads as one driver, but it splits into the company and the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Exuberant means full of energy and high spirits, a close synonym of vivacious.

clue.text: Part of supermarket is plugging beer

indicators.note: plugging means filling a hole, so these letters sit inside the word after

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
taken as written

explanation.surface: A store section is promoting a beer brand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plugging' suggests advertising, but it means filling a gap.
explanation.definitionFit: An aisle is a walkway between shelves, so it is one part of a shop's layout.

clue.text: Some undercover agents born too long ago

indicators.note: some means a portion, so only a run of letters within the next words is wanted

parts.note: the run of letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A few spies were born too early to be suitable for the job.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone over the age limit was born too early to qualify, which is the sense of being too old.

clue.text: Weird tapas dish served in Italian restaurant?

indicators.note: weird means strange or out of order, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: the five letters of the Spanish snack word are the fodder

explanation.surface: It would be odd for Spanish small plates to be offered at an Italian restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: Tapas are Spanish snacks; their scrambled letters make the Italian staple, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasta is the classic Italian food, so it is a natural dish to find on an Italian menu.

clue.text: Food spoiled every now and then

indicators.note: now and then means at intervals, so only every second letter is taken

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: Meals that go off from time to time.
explanation.definitionFit: A pie is a baked dish with pastry, a common kind of food.

clue.text: Goodbye features on Greatest Hits tracklist, perhaps

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a farewell wishing someone well

definitions.text: features on Greatest Hits tracklist, perhaps
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a compilation album contains every top song by the band

explanation.surface: A farewell song appears on a band's compilation album.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' flags that the second half is a playful description rather than a strict synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a common way of wishing someone well as they leave, and also describes every top song gathered together.
